translations.uiAbout-disclaimerHint-text: PortfoliGo is a game with fictional companies and prices and simplified rules – not investment advice.
translations.uiAbout-legalNotice-disclaimerGame: PortfoliGo is a game. Nothing in the app is investment advice or a recommendation to buy, hold or sell a security.
translations.uiAbout-legalNotice-disclaimerFictional: All companies, banks, exchanges, indices, funds and identifiers such as ISINs are fictional. Prices, dividends and interest are generated by a simulation. Regions and countries are real, but the prices say nothing about their markets.
translations.uiAbout-legalNotice-disclaimerSimplified: The rules are simplified, for example for taxes (a flat 25% without solidarity surcharge or church tax), fees and trading hours. What you win or lose in the game can’t be transferred to real investments.
translations.uiAbout-legalNotice-licensesIntro: PortfoliGo uses the following libraries and fonts. We thank their authors.
translations.uiAbout-legalNotice-tradingview: The price charts are drawn by TradingView Lightweight Charts™; the TradingView logo in the chart links to the maker.

translations.featureHelp-gameHelpPage-intro: The game’s terms as they apply in PortfoliGo. Some rules are simplified compared with reality.
translations.featureHelp-helpPage-intro: The game’s terms as they apply in PortfoliGo. Some rules are simplified compared with reality.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-depot-keywords: brokerage account securities account custody account depot Depot
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-depot-short: The account for your securities at a bank. Every brokerage account has its own settlement account, through which purchases, sales and income are booked.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-depot-details: You can open as many brokerage accounts as you like at any bank, instantly and free of charge. A brokerage account can only be closed when it’s empty and has no open orders or savings plans.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-clearingAccount-key: settlement account clearing account cash account Verrechnungskonto
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-clearingAccount-sho: The cash account of a brokerage account: purchases are paid from it, and sale proceeds, dividends and distributions are credited to it.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-clearingAccount-det: It has no arranged overdraft. It only goes into the red through charges by the bank such as the custody fee or interest, never through a purchase. While it’s in the red, new buy orders are blocked and debit interest accrues. The bank pays interest on the balance monthly, depending on its terms.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-currentAccount-keyw: current account checking account bank account Girokonto
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-currentAccount-shor: The account for everyday money: your salary comes in here and your living costs go out.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-currentAccount-deta: A current account pays no interest and, depending on the bank, costs a monthly account fee; some banks waive it once money comes in from outside (salary or starting capital). Brokers don’t offer current accounts.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-savingsAccount-keyw: instant-access savings account easy-access savings interest Tagesgeld
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-savingsAccount-shor: An interest-bearing account that you can transfer money into and withdraw it from at any time.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-savingsAccount-deta: The bank pays interest on the balance monthly or quarterly, depending on its terms; it counts as investment income. Direct banks usually pay more than high-street banks.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-salaryAccount-keywo: salary account wages living costs Gehaltskonto
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-salaryAccount-short: The current account your net salary is paid into and your living costs are paid from.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-salaryAccount-detai: The salary arrives on the last banking day of the month and living costs go out on the first, each at 06:00. You can change your salary account; the overdraft limit follows the salary payments.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-overdraft-keywords: overdraft arranged overdraft limit interest Dispo
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-overdraft-short: The amount by which you may overdraw your current account. You pay overdraft interest on the amount you use.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-overdraft-details: The limit depends on the salary payments received at the bank in the last three full months and is adjusted on the first banking day of each month. It applies to the current account of the bank with the most salary payments. Interest is calculated to the day and charged monthly.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-toleratedOverdraft-: unarranged overdraft beyond overdraft limit geduldete Überziehung
A negative balance beyond the overdraft limit. It has no upper limit but costs an interest surcharge.

It only happens through charges by the bank, such as living costs; your own transfers and standing orders only go up to the available amount. The part beyond the limit is charged the overdraft interest plus a surcharge. By default, the game then pauses (auto-pause).
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-standingOrder-short: A transfer between two of your accounts that runs automatically on the same day every month.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-standingOrder-detai: You choose a day from 1 to 28; if it isn’t a banking day, the order runs on the next one. It runs at 06:00 after salary, interest and living costs. If there isn’t enough available money, it’s skipped entirely for that month.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-orderTypes-short: Market buys or sells immediately, limit only at a price you set, stop only from a price threshold, and stop-limit combines both.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-orderTypes-details: You can place orders at any time. They are only executed while the instrument’s exchange is open; the game checks them every game minute. There are no partial executions.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-marketOrder-short: Executed immediately: a purchase at the ask price, a sale at the bid price. If the exchange is closed, at the next open.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-marketOrder-details: You don’t know in advance exactly at which price it will be executed. For a purchase, the game therefore reserves the estimated order value plus a 5% buffer.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-limitOrder-short: Buys only if the ask price is at most the limit, and sells only if the bid price reaches at least the limit.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-limitOrder-details: It is executed at the current ask or bid price, i.e. at the limit or better. If the price never reaches the limit, the order stays open until its validity ends.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-stopOrder-keywords: stop order stop-loss stop buy stop price Stop-Order
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-stopOrder-short: Becomes a market order as soon as the price reaches the stop threshold: a purchase when the ask rises to the stop, a sale when the bid falls to the stop.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-stopOrder-details: A sell stop limits losses (stop-loss). If the exchange opens with a price gap below the stop, the sale happens at the opening price, possibly well below the stop.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-stopLimitOrder-shor: Becomes a limit order with the limit you set once the stop threshold is reached.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-stopLimitOrder-deta: This protects you from an execution far below the stop. In return, the order may not be executed at all after it has been triggered.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-validity-keywords: validity good for day good till date good till cancelled expiry Gültigkeit
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-validity-short: How long an order stays active: good for day, good till date or good till cancelled.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-validity-details: ‘Good for day’ ends with the exchange’s next market close, ‘good till date’ at 24:00 on that date. ‘Good till cancelled’ also ends after one year at the latest. After that, the order expires and the reservation is released.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-reservation-short: Money that an open buy order earmarks on the settlement account. It is no longer available for other payments.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-reservation-details: Limit orders reserve the limit times the quantity plus costs, market and stop orders the estimated order value with a 5% buffer plus costs, and amount orders the amount. When the order is executed, cancelled or expires, the reservation is released.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-spread-keywords: spread bid ask bid price ask price Geldkurs Briefkurs
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-spread-short: The gap between the ask (buying price) and the bid (selling price). If you buy and sell again straight away, you lose it.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-spread-details: Small, volatile securities have a wider spread than large, stable ones; it widens when the underlying’s exchange is closed. Neobrokers trade through a market maker and add a small mark-up to the bid and ask. The game values positions at the bid price.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-fractionalShares-ke: fractional shares fractions fractional trading Bruchstücke
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-fractionalShares-sh: Parts of a stock or ETF smaller than one whole share, e.g. 0.25 shares.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-fractionalShares-de: Savings plans always buy fractional shares. Only neobrokers offer individual orders with fractional shares; you can sell fractional shares at any bank.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-savingsPlan-keyword: savings plan monthly instalment regular investing Sparplan
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-savingsPlan-short: Automatically buys an ETF or a stock for a fixed amount every month on the chosen day.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-savingsPlan-details: It is executed at the exchange’s market open on the execution day (1 to 28) or on the next trading day, always in fractional shares. The money comes from the brokerage account’s settlement account; if there isn’t enough, the execution is skipped. Not every security is available for savings plans.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-orderFee-keywords: order fee exchange fee costs transaction costs commission Ordergebühr
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-orderFee-short: The costs of an order: the bank’s order fee (fixed, percentage or both) and a fixed exchange fee.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-orderFee-details: The order ticket shows the costs before you submit. On a purchase they increase the acquisition cost, and on a sale they reduce the proceeds. Savings plans have their own costs and no exchange fee.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-custodyFee-keywords: custody fee account costs platform fee Depotgebühr
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-custodyFee-short: An annual fee some banks charge for keeping the brokerage account, often a percentage of the portfolio value with a minimum amount.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-custodyFee-details: It is debited quarterly from the settlement account on the first banking day for the past quarter, even if that takes the account into the red. Many direct banks and brokers don’t charge one.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-ter-keywords: TER total expense ratio ongoing charges OCF costs
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-ter-short: The ongoing costs of an ETF per year as a percentage. They aren’t debited but are included in the price.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-ter-details: The game deducts the TER from the fund’s value pro rata, day by day. An ETF with a TER of 0.2% therefore lags its index by about 0.2% a year.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-dividend-short: A part of the company’s profit that a stock pays out to its shareholders.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-dividend-details: The dividend is announced 20 trading days before the ex-date. It is credited to the settlement account and taxed like all investment income. Depending on the region, companies pay annually, semi-annually or quarterly.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-exDate-keywords: ex-date ex-dividend record date payment date pay date Ex-Tag
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-exDate-short: On the ex-date, the dividend is deducted from the price; it goes to whoever held the stock at the market close on the previous day. It’s paid two banking days later.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-exDate-details: So a purchase on the ex-date no longer gets the dividend, and a sale on the ex-date keeps it. Fractional shares receive it pro rata.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-etf-keywords: ETF exchange traded fund index fund tracker fund
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-etf-short: An exchange-traded fund that tracks an index. With one purchase, you invest in all constituents of the index at once.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-etf-details: The price follows the index minus the TER and a small deviation depending on the replication. Outside trading hours, the game shows an indicative value.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-distribution-keywor: distributing accumulating distribution accumulation income use dividends ausschüttend thesaurierend
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-distribution-short: A distributing ETF pays out the dividends of its constituents; an accumulating ETF reinvests them immediately.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-distribution-detail: Before costs and taxes, both earn almost the same. Distributions are credited to the settlement account and taxed immediately; the fund doesn’t announce their amount in advance.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-index-keywords: index price index total return index benchmark index Kursindex Performanceindex
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-index-short: A figure for the performance of a group of stocks, weighted by their market cap. A price index shows only the prices; a total return index reinvests the dividends.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-index-details: The weights of individual constituents are capped, and the composition stays fixed in the game. You can’t buy an index itself, but you can buy an ETF on it.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-capitalGainsTax-key: withholding tax capital gains tax tax investment income Abgeltungsteuer
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-capitalGainsTax-sho: In the game, a flat 25% applies to investment income above the saver’s allowance, without solidarity surcharge or church tax.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-capitalGainsTax-det: Investment income is interest, dividends, distributions and price gains minus price losses. The bank withholds the tax immediately on every item of income and refunds it immediately when a later loss reduces it.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-saverAllowance-keyw: saver’s allowance tax-free allowance exemption order Sparerpauschbetrag
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-saverAllowance-shor: Up to €1,000 of investment income a year remains tax-free. Whatever you don’t use expires at the end of the year.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-saverAllowance-deta: In the game, it applies automatically to all banks together; no exemption order is needed.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-lossPot-keywords: loss pot loss carryforward loss offsetting Verlusttopf
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-lossPot-short: Losses are offset against later income. If the year ends in the red, the loss is carried forward to the next year.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-lossPot-details: As a simplification, the game has a single pot for all income across all banks: stock losses also reduce the tax on interest and dividends. The carryforward doesn’t expire.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-lotFifo-keywords: lot lots FIFO first in first out cost price acquisition cost
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-lotFifo-short: Every purchase is a lot with its own acquisition cost. Sales follow FIFO: the shares bought first are sold first.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-lotFifo-details: The acquisition cost includes the purchase costs; the cost price is the acquisition cost divided by the quantity. The realised gain is the proceeds after costs minus the acquisition cost of the shares sold.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-netWorth-short: All account balances (a negative balance counts as negative) plus the value of your securities at the bid price.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-netWorth-details: Salary and living costs change it just as price movements do. That’s why the time-weighted return shows how well you’ve invested.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-twr-keywords: TWR time-weighted return performance zeitgewichtete Rendite
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-twr-short: The return on your net worth without the effect of salary and living costs. It measures only how your invested money has performed.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-twr-details: The game calculates the return for each day after inflows and outflows and chains the days together. Interest, fees, taxes and dividends count towards the return. It is only annualised after 365 days.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-benchmark-short: A comparison portfolio that puts all money into the world total return index without costs or taxes. It shows you whether you beat the market.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-benchmark-details: Starting capital and every net inflow are bought at the daily close. The second comparison, ‘Without investing’, shows what you would have if everything had stayed in the salary account.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-volatility-short: How much a price fluctuates: the standard deviation of the daily returns over the last 252 trading days, annualised.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-volatility-details: Higher volatility means larger swings in both directions.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-beta-short: How strongly a security moves with the market on average. A beta of 1 moves like the world price index, 1.5 half as much again, 0.5 half as much.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-beta-details: Calculated from the daily returns over the last 252 trading days compared with the world price index.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-marketCap-keywords: market capitalisation market cap market value Marktkapitalisierung
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-marketCap-short: A company’s market cap: the number of shares times the price.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-marketCap-details: The index weights are based on the market cap of the freely tradable shares. ETFs show their fund size instead.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-savingsRate-keyword: savings rate saving income spending Sparquote
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-savingsRate-short: The share of your income in a month that is left over after all spending.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-savingsRate-details: Income is earnings, interest and dividends; spending is living costs, fees, debit interest and taxes. Transfers between your own accounts don’t count. The rate can be negative.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-tradingHours-keywor: trading hours market hours exchange open closed Handelszeiten
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-tradingHours-short: Exchanges trade only at fixed times on weekdays: Asia-Pacific 01:00–07:00, Europe 09:00–17:30, North America 15:30–22:00 game time.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-tradingHours-detail: Emerging markets have their own hours per exchange. Everything is closed at weekends; there are no public holidays in the game. Outside trading hours, the bank accepts orders and executes them at the next open.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-gameSpeed-keywords: game speed speed tempo faster slower Spielgeschwindigkeit
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-gameSpeed-short: How fast game time runs: from real time up to one week per second. Pause stops it.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-gameSpeed-details: The game starts paused on Monday, 1 April 2030. At high speeds, salary, interest, orders and prices work exactly as in real time, only faster.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-jump-short: Runs game time at high speed to the next market open, the start of the next month or a date, at most one year ahead.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-jump-details: Everything is processed as in normal play. You can cancel the fast-forward; an auto-pause ends it.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-autoPause-short: The game stops by itself on important events, by default when the overdraft limit is exceeded.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-autoPause-details: In the settings, you decide for each event whether it pauses the game. The auto-pause also applies while fast-forwarding, but never during the catch-up after opening the app.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-backgroundModes-sho: What game time does when you leave the app: keep running in real time, pause, or keep running at the selected or a custom speed.
translations.uiHelp-glossaryTexts-backgroundModes-det: When the app is closed, time keeps running in real time, except in the ‘Pause’ mode, and is caught up the next time you open it. Optionally, the game pauses after a set time in the background.

translations.featurePwa-pwaEffects-installed: PortfoliGo is now installed as an app.
translations.uiPwa-appSettings-installed: PortfoliGo is installed on this device.
translations.uiPwa-appSettings-installPrompt: Once installed, PortfoliGo starts like a separate application, works offline too, and the browser is less likely to delete your games.
translations.uiPwa-appSettings-installIos: Tap ‘Share’ and then ‘Add to Home Screen’. When started as an app from the Home Screen, Safari doesn’t delete your games after seven days without a visit.
translations.uiPwa-appSettings-installUnavailable: The browser isn’t offering the installation right now. In Chrome and Edge, it’s in the menu under ‘Install app’; in Safari on the Mac, under ‘File’ → ‘Add to Dock’.
translations.uiPwa-appSettings-notificationsText: Shows the events whose ‘Browser’ column is switched on as system notifications while PortfoliGo is running in a background tab or another window. On smartphones, the system suspends the app in the background, so they rarely appear there.
translations.uiPwa-appSettings-storageText: Games are stored only in this browser. The browser doesn’t delete persistently stored data when space runs low; installed as an app, it’s protected even better.
translations.uiPwa-appSettings-permissionDenied: Denied – can be changed in the browser’s site settings
translations.uiPwa-preReleaseHint-text: Before version 1.0, updates can make games invalid. Export your game regularly.
translations.uiPwa-updateBanner-versionReadyText: It becomes active the next time you start the app. Before version 1.0, it can make games invalid.
translations.uiPwa-updateBanner-unrecoverable: The stored version of the app is damaged.

translations.featureSettings-settingsPage-deviceHint: Applies to all players in this browser and is not exported.
translations.featureSettings-settingsPage-playerHint: Belongs to the game and is exported with the player.
translations.featureSettings-settingsEffects-saveFail: The setting only applies until the next reload because the storage is full. Export your game and delete old players; the settings show the storage used under ‘App’.
The setting only applies until the next reload because it couldn’t be saved on this device.
translations.uiSettings-autoPauseSettings-hint: The game stops when one of these events occurs while the app is visible – also while fast-forwarding. When the app is hidden, this only applies if the game runs there at the selected or a custom speed. Otherwise, and during the catch-up, it keeps running; the events then appear in the absence report.
translations.uiSettings-deviceSettings-languageHint: The app reloads when you switch. Numbers and dates follow the language; amounts stay in euros.
translations.uiSettings-deviceSettings-changeColorsHi: Sign and arrow always show the direction as well. Example:
translations.uiSettings-deviceSettings-priceHighlight: Changed prices briefly light up in the colour for gains or losses. If ‘Reduce motion’ is set on the device, this never happens.
translations.uiSettings-deviceSettings-shortcutsHintP: Control the game time and open the command palette without a mouse. The shortcuts without Ctrl don’t work while an input field or control has focus.
translations.uiSettings-notificationChannelSettings-h: Every event appears in the notification centre. Here you choose which ones are also shown briefly as a pop-up and which ones the browser reports while the app is hidden – this only works if you allow it in the browser.
translations.uiSettings-playerProfile-seedHint: The same seed creates the same world: the same banks, securities and price histories. Share it so that others can play in your world.
translations.uiSettings-playerSettings-backgroundHint: If the app is closed or frozen by the browser, it only catches up in real time the next time you open it. Fast speeds in the background drain the battery.
translations.uiSettings-playerSettings-realtimeHint: When the app is hidden or closed, game time keeps running at 1 s/s. It is caught up the next time you open the app.
translations.uiSettings-playerSettings-pauseHint: When the app is hidden or closed, game time stands still. Afterwards it continues without a catch-up.
translations.uiSettings-playerSettings-keepSpeedHint: When the app is hidden, game time keeps running as fast as currently selected.
translations.uiSettings-playerSettings-customSpeedHin: When the app is hidden, game time runs at the speed you choose here.

translations.featureTaxes-taxesPage-ruleRate: Investment income is taxed at {$INTERPOLATION} to the extent that it exceeds the saver’s allowance of {$INTERPOLATION_1} in a year.
translations.featureTaxes-taxesPage-rulePool: Interest, dividends, distributions and gains and losses from sales go into one shared pot, across all banks.
translations.featureTaxes-taxesPage-ruleWithholding: The tax is withheld immediately on every gain or income; a later loss in the same year refunds it.
translations.featureTaxes-taxesPage-ruleCarryForward: If the year ends with a loss, it’s carried into the next year as a loss carryforward. An unused saver’s allowance expires at the end of the year.
